speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) whether the Government intends to take into account the Environmental Impact Study that was undertaken during the development of the former Keppel Club site, which found ecological connectivity for birds between the Southern Ridges and Labrador Nature Reserve, when conducting environmental studies of the proposed development of Gillman Barracks; and (b) if so, how will the Ministry ensure that any future development of Gillman Barracks will not significantly compromise this important ecological connectivity.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) whether rejuvenation plans for Gillman Barracks that were announced by the Singapore Land Authority in 2022 will be taken into account when studying the future development of Gillman Barracks; and (b) whether the environmental and heritage studies commissioned for the potential development of the area will be accessible to environmental groups and the wider public.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: First is, in terms of the previous environmental impact assessments that were done, which found a significant ecological connectivity between the Keppel Club site and also the Southern Ridges and Labrador Nature Reserve site.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: The EIS for the nearby Keppel Club site found that even with mitigation measures, redevelopment could have major residual impact on biodiversity due to permanent habitat loss and fragmentation.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: In light of this, can the Minister clarify what specific plans are in place to designate sizeable core habitat patches and green corridors within Gillman Barracks to maintain landscape connectivity between the Labrador Nature Reserve, the Southern Ridges and the Greater Southern Waterfront?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: If there are no such plans, how does the Government intend to prevent critical ecological linkages from being irreversibly compromised?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I also heard the Minister mention earlier that the existing tenants whose leases will run out progressively until 2030, will not be affected if the plans to redevelop the site goes ahead at Gillman Barracks.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: However, I anticipate that there will be some new tenants who might come in and can the Minister confirm whether the leases will run beyond 2030?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: And also, will help be given to these tenants who come in a bit later, especially during the rejuvenation period?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Will there be help given to them to find new leases elsewhere if the redevelopment plans actually do go through?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: And finally, my last supplementary question is, I think the Minister mentioned earlier that there will be certain heritage and environmental impact assessments also carried out and that these will be made available.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Can I ask whether the reports will eventually be made available in full for the public, because I understand that sometimes these are only made available in a redacted form.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: So, can I ask whether these will be made available in full?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And we will make sure that that ecological connectivity is provided for, in the surroundings of the Keppel Golf Course.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On lease, as I have said, the site had been made available for interim use since the 1990s.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The existing tenancies will progressively expire by 2030.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Thereafter, we will plan for the entire site, including residential as well as the commercial uses of the site.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And so, at that point in time, we will engage the tenants, engage future tenants as far as the commercial use of the site is concerned.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As with all these studies, they come in large volumes with lots and lots of technical detail.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will make sure that what we put out is meaningful for members of the public as well as experts to be able to understand and comment on.
